items.title: Fake Web3 Accelerator Uses Malicious npm Packages to Target Crypto Founders
items.description: A fake Web3 accelerator called Apex has been using malicious npm packages to target cryptocurrency start-ups and founders with what appeared to be free AI credits, coding tools, smart-contract audits, investment access, and invitations to in-person events. Behind the polished Web3 pitch, the operation delivered malware for macOS and Windows, exposed AI-agent data to attacker-run […] The post…

items.title: Anthropic Warns AI Models Could Soon Self-Replicate on Smart TVs and IoT Devices Without a Data Center
items.description: Anthropic warns that small AI models may be months away from self-replicating across poorly secured smart TVs and other internet-connected devices. Its research suggests future AI worms could run on consumer hardware rather than depend on a data center, making them harder to shut down through a single central service. items.title: Small AI Models May Soon Be Able to Self-Replicate on IoT Devices, Anthropic Warns
items.description: Experiments show cheap TV boxes can run capable AI models, and small models may soon be able to spread across such devices on their own. The post Small AI Models May Soon Be Able to Self-Replicate on IoT Devices, Anthropic Warns appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: XWorm RAT Evolves Into Surveillance Platform
items.description: Expanded plugin count allows the malware to monitor users’ location, stream live audio, and interact with authenticated browser sessions. The post XWorm RAT Evolves Into Surveillance Platform appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: LG Smart TVs Vulnerable to Pre-Auth Root Takeover From Local Network
items.description: Three vulnerabilities in LG's webOS can be chained to give an attacker on the same local network root access to certain smart TVs without a PIN or any interaction from the owner. LG has issued a fix, according to an advisory published by SSD Secure Disclosure on October 12. The chain was tested on two TV models, the 32LQ636BPSA and the 27TQ600SW, running webOS 7.5.7-25 on firmware

items.title: npm Trusted Publishing Flaw With 10 Million Downloads Exposes 1,500+ Packages to Malicious Takeover
items.description: A security flaw in npm’s Trusted Publishing feature exposed more than 1,500 packages to possible takeover through reclaimed GitHub repository names. The affected packages accounted for more than 10 million total downloads and over one million downloads per month, creating a serious software supply-chain risk for developers, CI/CD systems, and organizations that rely on npm […] The post npm…

items.title: Hackers Exploit Citrix NetScaler 0-Days to Deploy Platypus Remote Access Tool
items.description: Threat actors are exploiting two critical Citrix NetScaler zero-day vulnerabilities to deploy a modified Platypus remote access tool on exposed ADC and Gateway appliances. The activity shows how quickly attackers are moving from initial access to persistent control of edge devices that often sit between corporate networks and the public internet. The campaign targets CVE-2026-88771 […] The post…

items.title: Product Walkthrough: Bitdefender AI Visibility and Control
items.description: A user opens a browser tab, pastes data into a chat assistant, and nothing is installed. A developer adds a coding assistant as an editor extension, and nothing shows up in the installed programs list. items.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
items.description: Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets on the night of October 11 and warmed them, forcing stores to throw food away, several retail chains said. The attackers reached them through the controller that runs all of a store's fridges and freezers, a device made by Danish company Danfoss that maintenance firms can manage remotely.
